Jordan,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and the DPA scaffolding. Our legal team ran a pass and attached tracked redlines for the Data Processing Addendum and the SCCs. The key asks from our side are summarized below so you can route to the right owners: 

- Stronger liability carveouts around cross-border transfers (we prefer explicit transfer impact addendum language and indemnities for regulatory fines).

We appreciate a consolidated response with proposed alternative language. We can stand up a short call next week if helpful.

Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme legal - initial DPA redlines

Jordan / team,

I reviewed Acme's tracked changes and sketched a negotiation memo + redline summary. Key points below (high-level recommendations in bold). See attached for a single consolidated tracked-document.

1) Liability & Fines
- Acme requests indemnity for regulatory fines stemming from transfers. We should decline broad indemnities. Instead: (a) accept obligation to assist and remediate; (b) offer limited cooperation indemnity where Redwood's gross negligence caused a fine.
- Proposed language: 'Redwood shall not be liable for third-party fines arising solely from Customer's instructions or Customer's failure to comply with applicable law.'

2) Data Subject Requests (DSRs)
- Acme asked: 15 days for erasure/portability, 30 days for complex requests. Operationally 15 days is tight for complex flows that involve subprocessors. Recommend: accept 15 days for straightforward requests; 30 days for complex, with good-faith extensions for subprocessors. Add a commitment to provide a "DSR assistance playbook" (samples and contacts).

3) Encryption / KMS
- Acme wants per-customer (BYOK) KMS control. We can offer two options: (A) Managed keys with logical separation and audit logs (default), (B) Enterprise BYOK available on Redwood Private/Dedicated with a surcharge and operational onboarding.
- Need Ben to confirm operational feasibility and pricing delta.

4) Backups & Deletion
- Acme's 7–14 day delete window is operationally unrealistic. Recommend: accept deletion of live data within 30 days of effective deletion request; backups purged within 90 days (with an operational carveout for legal holds). Spell out the retention exceptions.

5) SCCs & Transfer Impact Addendum
- We should accept SCCs as baseline and propose a Transfer Impact Addendum that documents: (i) hosting regions, (ii) subprocessors list and categories, (iii) mitigations like encryption in transit/rest, and (iv) fallback routing where possible. Push back on any binding operational guarantees that are infrastructure-level (eg. absolute geo-fencing) unless Customer subscribes to Private/Dedicated.

6) Evidence & Auditability
- Offer to provide SOC2/ISO summaries and an ops evidence package under an NDA. Ben — can you attach the ops stub (certificate summary + sample logs) to the consolidated reply?

Deliverables and next steps:
- I'll attach consolidated redline: Redwood_DPA_consolidated_redlines.docx
- Ben to confirm KMS options + ops evidence and call out required SOW/pricing for BYOK.
- Jordan to confirm whether procurement will accept the 30/90 retention windows or insist on a different route.

If procurement pushes hard on the 7–14 day backup deletion or on an indemnity for transfers, escalate to me and Karthik.

Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_consolidated_redlines.docx (DOCX, 98KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-01T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Acme legal - initial DPA redlines — operational notes

Team,

Quick ops reality check on the asks:

- Backups: We cannot promise sub-30-day guaranteed purge windows for backups without a special retention workflow. Backups are immutable for a period for disaster recovery. Proposed standard language: 'Live data will be deleted within 30 days after confirmed deletion; backups will be overwritten or purged in line with our backup rotation (not to exceed 90 days), except where retention is required by law or legal hold.'

- KMS/BYOK: BYOK can be supported on Dedicated and Private offerings only. For the hosted API we can provide customer-scoped keys with audit logs but not HSM-backed customer-owned keys by default. BYOK onboarding requires an ops runbook and a one-time setup fee.

- DSRs: We can meet 15-day basic SLAs for straightforward requests. For complex aggregations spanning multiple systems/subprocessors we need 30 days and the right to request reasonable clarification from the requester.

- Evidence: I'll attach an ops stub (certificate excerpt, sample access log format) under NDA. We'll include an internal runbook entry that details the timeline and the SOW/pricing options for BYOK.

I attached a zip with the stub evidence for legal to reference. If we go for BYOK, ops will need a 6–8 week implementation runway for onboarding for an enterprise customer.

Attachments: ops-evidence-stub.zip (ZIP, 2MB)

- Ben
Ben Carter | Director, Platform Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Acme legal - initial DPA redlines — consolidated response and next steps

Harriet,

Thanks for the redlines and the patience — appreciate the clear asks. We reviewed and consolidated our position. Summary of what Redwood is proposing (high level):

1) Transfers & SCCs: We accept the SCCs as the baseline. Instead of a broad indemnity for cross-border regulatory fines, Redwood will: (a) commit to a Transfer Impact Addendum that documents hosting regions, subprocessors and mitigations; (b) agree to reasonable cooperation and remediation; (c) accept limited indemnity only in cases of Redwood's gross negligence.

2) DSR SLA: We can meet 15-day SLAs for routine erasure/portability requests and 30 days for requests requiring subprocessor coordination. We'll include a DSR assistance playbook and a named escalation contact.

3) KMS options: For hosted accounts we provide customer-scoped managed keys with audit logs. BYOK (customer-held keys/HSM-backed) is available on Dedicated/Private with an implementation onboarding (6–8 weeks) and an associated surcharge. We'll include the ops SOW language in the order form if Acme opts in.

4) Backups & Deletion: Proposed operational language — live-data deletion within 30 days; backups purged in line with backup rotation (not exceeding 90 days), except where retention is required by law or legal hold. We cannot accept a guaranteed 7–14 day backup purge.

5) Evidence & Auditability: We'll provide SOC2 summary reports and an ops evidence package under NDA. Ben attached the ops stub in our internal thread.

Next steps: Attached is our consolidated tracked redline (Redwood_DPA_consolidated_redlines.docx). If Acme is comfortable with this package, we can publish a Transfer Impact Addendum and push the DPA + Order Form to DocuSign.
